data.claim: A shared glob is exempt from per-task lease collisions
data.falsifier: a knob task still refused on the defaults path
data.mechanism: lease code skips shared_globs; WIRING only adds the glob to task globs
data.probe_output: fails without the config entry (1 failed), 10 passed with it
data.question: Does listing the packaged defaults in [lease].shared_globs and dropping it from WIRING['knob'] stop knob tasks leasing it?

evidence.note: research note recorded, CONFIRMED; new test fails without the shared_globs entry
r-adapters n/a; r-everything-configurable: shared_globs is an existing knob; no new knob
config.toml shared_globs + wiring.py + tests; 10 tests pass

chunk_findings.detail: The new test only reads `.ddflow/config.toml` and checks that two strings appear in `lease.shared_globs`; it does not exercise the stated acceptance condition that two knob tasks can claim and merge concurrently, nor the stated falsifier that a knob task still gets a lease refusal on the defaults path. For example, if `lease.claim` still refuses a task that touches `ddflow/templates/default.toml` because the path is no longer in `WIRING['knob']` and `shared_globs` is only consulted for already-declared task globs, two knob tasks in different sections will still block, but this test will pass because the config file contains the expected strings. Thus the change has no regression test for the 15-hour `default.toml` block it claims to close.
